text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mostly firmer in a market closely watching New York's March expiry. At the close May was up $1.40 at $309.50 per tonne, while August closed $1.10 higher at $308.90 per tonne. London's March contract expired earlier this month, while New York's spot raws contract expired at the close of CSCE business on Friday.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed higher in volatile trade as the nearby spread swelled to a 40 point premium in March before ending at a 35 point premium. The March contract went off the board at 11.32 cents/lb, up 27 points from the previous close.

May added 8 points to close at 10.97 cents/lb, while the outer months gained between 2 and 6 points. The latest ISO's estimate of supply and demand in 1996/97 had no impact on prices as it was very much in line with expectations.

INTERNATIONAL - According to the International Sugar Organization in London world sugar production in 1996/97 (October/September) should reach 123.34 million tonnes, raw value, which compares to our September/August figure of 123.3 million tonnes. 1995/96 production was put at 123.90 million tonnes. The ISO forecast a world sugar surplus of 2.80 million tonnes for 1996/97, which was sharply lower than the 1995/96 figure of 5.94 million tonnes.

World sugar consumption in 1996/97 was estimated at 120.54 million tonnes after 117.96 million tonnes a year earlier. Our latest estimate for September/August 1996/97 was for a total of 120.3 million tonnes, up from 116.9 million tonnes in 1995/96. The ISO cut its 1996/97 production figure for India by 800,000 tonnes to 15.50 million tonnes, while the Cuban figure was lowered by 250,000 tonnes to 4.80 million tonnes.

Thai production in 1996/97 is expected to reach 6.50 million tonnes, 125,000 tonnes lower than the December estimate but above the 6.38 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. The forecast for Brazil's sugar output was left unchanged at 13.50 million tonnes, while a new production record of 5.70 million tonnes was forecast for Australia as a result of a 5 per cent rise in cane areas.

The ISO said the projected 1996/97 surplus should not be regarded in isolation as the 1995/96 crop year also saw a surplus. It was added that it must be reminded that a surplus of 5.9 million tonnes resulted from the 1995/96 crop cycle and therefore the combined surplus over the two crop cycles as a substantial 8.7 million tonnes.
It was emphasized that even if a high proportion of the surplus is locked up in India, there is no doubt that the world sugar economy suffers from a large stock overhang, not seen since 1991/92.

THAILAND - According to the Ministry of Industry sugar production in 1996/97 should reach 6.545 million tonnes, raw value, up from 6.323 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. Consumption in 1996/97 is estimated to reach 1.804 million tonnes, up from 1.707 million tonnes the previous year.

According to preliminary figures sugar exports in January 1997 jumped to 448,600 tonnes, raw value, from 379,700 tonnes exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 up to 504,200 tonnes, nearly 11 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995/96. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (November/October) reached 4.7 million tonnes, up from 3.9 million tonnes exported in 1994/95.

BRAZIL - Sugar production in the period from May to February 16 amounted to a total of 14.306 million tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 13.413 million tonnes. Production in the Center South where the campaign draws to a close in December was 11.317 million tonnes compared to 10.177 million tonnes, while the North/Northeast so far produced 2.989 million tonnes against 3.236 million tonnes.

Alcohol production in the same period reached 14.056 billion litres, up from 12.478 billion litres in the like period the previous year. Production in the Center South amounted to 12.107 billion litres (10.908 billion litres) while output in the North/Northeast reached 1.949 billion litres (1.571 billion litres).
Total production of anhydrous alcohol rose to 4.484 billion litres (2.958 billion litres) while hydrous alcohol production was 9.571 billion litres (9.521 billion litres).

SOUTH KOREA - Sugar imports in October 1996 amounted to 118,096 tonnes, raw value, against 120,575 tonnes in October 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1996 (January/October) up to 1.168 million tonnes against 1.113 million tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1995 amounted to 1.306 million tonnes compared to 1.275 million tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/October 1996 were Thailand with 628,557 tonnes raws against 352,912 tonnes and Australia with 494,670 tonnes, up from 533,524 tonnes. Sugar exports in October 1996 amounted to 22,332 tonnes, up from 28,673 tonnes exported in October 1995.

This brought cumulative exports in January/October 1996 up 249,846 tonnes compared to 217,742 tonnes in 1995. Total exports in 1995 reached 247,235 tonnes against 297,572 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in January/October 1996 were Hong Kong with 110,592 tonnes whites against 100,377 tonnes and Indonesia with 46,836 tonnes compared to 34,249 tonnes.
